standard_prerequisites.use: Derived categories of quasi-coherent sheaves, pseudo-coherent complexes, the derived Chow lemma, flat proper pseudo-coherent direct images, and detection of pseudo-coherence on projective space. These are cited prerequisites; the base-change computation, the Fourier-Mukai identification and the final reduction are retained in the author's proof.

core_obligations: Construct the setup from the derived Chow lemma for a given point x, and identify RGamma(P^n_A, Rq_*(Lp^*K tensor E) tensor O(i)) with RGamma(X, K tensor Rp_*(E tensor Lq^*O(i))) by base change.
Use pseudo-coherence of Rp_*(E tensor Lq^*O(i)) on X and the hypothesis to get pseudo-coherence on projective space, then convert back and restrict to conclude relative pseudo-coherence of K|_U.

proof_roadmap.step: Fix x in X, obtain U, n, V, Z, z, E from the derived Chow lemma, set up the projections p and q, and prove the three-term chain of equalities for RGamma(P^n_A, Rq_*(Lp^*K tensor E) tensor O(i)).
Deduce pseudo-coherence on projective space, identify Rq_*(Lp^*K tensor E)|_{X x_A V} with R(U -> V)_* K|_U, and conclude relative pseudo-coherence of K|_U from the on-charts criterion.

difficulty_reason: The lemma turns a condition on the derived global sections RGamma(X, E tensor K) for every pseudo-coherent E into relative pseudo-coherence of K itself, which is a genuinely dual statement. The proof picks a point x, invokes the derived Chow lemma to get a diagram U, n, V, Z, z, E, then computes a chain of three isomorphisms identifying RGamma(P^n_A, Rq_*(Lp^*K tensor E) tensor O(i)) with RGamma(X, K tensor Rp_*(E tensor Lq^*O(i))). Pseudo-coherence of the middle object follows from the hypothesis once one knows Rp_*(E tensor Lq^*O(i)) is pseudo-coherent on X, which needs the flat proper pseudo-coherent direct image theorem, and pseudo-coherence on projective space is then converted back to pseudo-coherence of Rq_*(Lp^*K tensor E). The last step restricts along X x_A V and uses the Fourier-Mukai computation to read off pseudo-coherence of K|_U relative to A. What is not routine is assembling the base-change isomorphism, the direct-image input and the projective-space detection into that single chain.
